_about: Dough recipes in baker's percentages: every part is a percentage of the total flour weight. Parts marked flour add up to 100. ball = grams per dough ball. shape = how the base is opened: hand (pressed out, then stretched with two fingers), roll (rolling pin or sheeter), press (pushed into a pan). R = target radius in bench units, size_cm = the real diameter that represents, crust_cm = width of raised rim to leave. bake = oven time multiplier. top = how much sauce, cheese and topping this size takes compared with a 30 cm pizza.

neapolitan.name: Neapolitan
neapolitan.desc: Soft, wet dough. Press it out leaving a rim, then stretch by hand for a puffy, charred crust.

ny.name: New York
ny.desc: Strong flour with a little oil and sugar. Big, thin, foldable, with a modest rim.

roman.name: Roman thin
roman.desc: Drier dough with oil, rolled flat with a pin. Paper-thin, no rim, cracker-crisp.

pan.name: Deep pan
pan.desc: Very wet dough pressed into an oiled pan. Thick and fluffy, and it takes longer to bake.

wholemeal.name: Wholemeal
wholemeal.desc: A 70/30 blend with wholemeal. Nutty, thirsty dough that needs more water.

glutenfree.name: Gluten-free
glutenfree.desc: More of a batter than a dough. It cannot be stretched, so it is pressed into a pan.
